scope: source/code/table audit plus post-hoc A16 same-population diagnostic; no new atlas or simulator fit

fu_s_current_contract.question: Does a boundary-correct implementation change the fitted two-population parameters and their support relative to the literal script?
fu_s_current_contract.data: batch1 mouse-level clone sizes, support n >= 2, mutant RFP cohorts kras1w/kras2w/kras4w
fu_s_current_contract.implementations: literal and boundary-correct Gillespie from EN6, unchanged
fu_s_current_contract.fitting: simulated-likelihood on a fixed grid: fs in {0.04,0.08,0.12,0.16,0.20}, sigma_f in {2,4,6,8,10,12,14}/7 x 2, sigma_s in {0.5,1.0,1.5,2.0}/7 x 2, r = q in {0.5,0.6,0.7,0.8}; 20 replicates x 2000 clones per grid point, seed 20260930; score = mean per-mouse multinomial log likelihood of the binned size distribution (bins 2,3,4,5-6,7-10,11-20,21-50,51+) with leave-one-mouse-out held-out scoring
fu_s_current_contract.comparison: best grid point per implementation, its held-out score, and the batch1 shifted-negative-binomial held-out score on the same bins
fu_s_current_contract.boundary: A coarse grid is not a maximum-likelihood fit; merger and segmentation of imaged clones are not modelled; agreement with the published curves is not evidence that a particular implementation produced them.

limitations: Cell cache and labels are existing exposed outputs, not independent data.
Same-population diagnostic keeps outcome-informed clusters and does not resolve overconditioning.
SMD ratios use different denominators; they are not fractions of signal explained.
No official claim grade was changed.
